items.title: Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee Series Events (1)
items.description:
On 12 April 2026 at 3:30 pm, the Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee held a visit to Sunnybank RSL Sub Branch. More than 30 representatives from member organisations took part.

The event was hosted by Lewis Lee OAM. Harry Claasen OAM, Vice President of Sunnybank RSL Sub Branch, gave a welcome address and introduced the history and development of Sunnybank RSL. Lewis Lee OAM, Chairman of the Australia Chinese Ex-Services Monument Committee, then spoke in detail about the history of Chinese Australian servicemen and women and the background to the establishment of the Chinese Australian war memorial. Through his presentation, participants gained a deep appreciation of the outstanding contributions of Chinese forebears to Australia; attendees paid silent tribute and lit candles in turn. Lewis Lee OAM later presented certificates of appreciation to community members who had contributed to the Australia Chinese Ex-Services Monument Committee.

During the program, Parnam Singh Heir, Chairman of the Australia Indian Ex-Services Monument Committee, also introduced the history of the Australia Indian war memorial, fostering mutual understanding and respect among different communities.

QCAC Chairman Peter Zhuang expressed sincere thanks to Lewis Lee OAM and Sunnybank RSL in his remarks, and invited everyone to attend the ANZAC Day commemoration to be held at Sunnybank RSL on 25 April.

As an important representative body for the Chinese community, the Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee maintains close communication with federal, state, and local government and is committed to voicing community concerns and advancing their expression and implementation.

items.title: Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee Series Events (2)
items.description:
On 5 May 2026, the Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee organised a delegation of member representatives to visit Brisbane City Hall and meet with Lord Mayor Adrian Schrinner and his team. Also present were Nathan Percy, Director of City Business for the Lord Mayor, and adviser Eddie Stephens.

During the meeting, QCAC Chairman Yongxin Zhuang introduced the committee’s background, mission, and development to the Lord Mayor. Delegates each gave a brief self-introduction. The Lord Mayor warmly welcomed the visit, delivered an address, and engaged in in-depth discussion on issues of shared concern.

During the visit, Mr Zhuang, on behalf of Deputy Secretary-General Yin Zhao, made a donation to the Lord Mayor’s Charitable Trust. The committee also presented a commemorative gift to the Lord Mayor as a gesture of sincere thanks and goodwill.

After the meeting, all participants posed for a group photo with the Lord Mayor.

The Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee will continue to host diverse programs that build bridges between the Chinese community and government at all levels, foster understanding and cooperation, and support the community’s prosperity and growth.

Sunnybank Chamber of Commerce was established in 2012, originated in Sunnybank and remains centered around Sunnybank's neighbouring suburbs.

It is a non-profit organization made up of established & emerging entrepreneurs from all industries who are dedicated to constant learning, growth & best business practice.

Sunnybank Chambers of Commerce are the voice of business community to local, State and Federal Governments.
